system.name: Enso
system.one_liner: a streaming interface for NIC-application communication that replaces fixed-size descriptors with dynamically sized, on-demand data streams

components.name: Metadata
components.role: incoming metadata for an RX operation, including the Enso Pipe ID and enqueued data size

components.name: Data
components.role: incoming raw data received by the NIC

components.name: RX Ensō Pipe Manager 1
components.role: one of 16 parallel per-pipe managers handling metadata for its assigned Enso Pipe

components.name: RX Ensō Pipe Manager 16
components.role: another parallel per-pipe manager (up to 16 total, elided in the figure)

components.name: MMIO/JTAG
components.role: configuration/control interface into each Pipe Manager and the Notification Buffer Manager

components.name: RX Notification Buffer Manager
components.role: aggregates metadata/notifications from the pipe managers and forwards them to the DMA engine

components.name: Data FIFO
components.role: buffers incoming data separately from metadata before it reaches the DMA engine, keeping inter-module queues small

components.name: DMA Engine
components.role: transfers the metadata/notification stream and the data stream into host memory

content.key_idea: The RX datapath demultiplexes incoming metadata across 16 parallel per-pipe managers, remultiplexes their output into a shared notification buffer manager, and separately FIFOs the raw data, before both reach the DMA engine.
content.reading_order: Left to right: Metadata and Data inputs fan out to 16 parallel Pipe Managers (metadata) and a Data FIFO (data), converging through the Notification Buffer Manager into the DMA Engine.

Metadata is handled separately from the data, which allows for smaller queues between modules.

summary: This figure shows Enso's NIC RX datapath, the hardware pipeline that receives data and metadata from the network before handing them to the host. Incoming Metadata (including the Enso Pipe ID and enqueued size) fans out to 16 parallel RX Enso Pipe Manager instances, each configurable via MMIO/JTAG, which process per-pipe state before their outputs are remultiplexed into a shared RX Notification Buffer Manager. Enso keeps the bulk Data path separate from metadata, running it through its own Data FIFO so that inter-module queues can stay small. Both the resulting Metadata/Notification stream and the buffered Data stream are finally handed to the DMA Engine, which moves them into host memory; the caption notes that a transfer crossing an Enso Pipe boundary is automatically split into several transfers no larger than the buffer size.
